slides.heading: Reveal Minesweeper
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Reveal Minesweeper, a medium recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Clicking a mine sets it to "X"; clicking a hidden cell reveals its adjacent-mine count and, if zero, recursively reveals neighbours.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Board of "M" (mine), "H" (hidden), "0"-"8" (revealed). Clicking a mine sets it to "X"; clicking a hidden cell reveals its adjacent-mine count and, if zero, recursively reveals neighbours.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Clicking a mine ends the game; clicking an empty square reveals neighbours recursively.
slides.narration: Clicking a mine ends the game; clicking an empty square reveals neighbours recursively.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Click a mine → X and stop
slides.narration: If the click is a mine, mark it and stop. Otherwise count adjacent mines; if there are none, recursively reveal every neighbour. Each cell is revealed at most once.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, if a mine, mark X. Second, count adjacent mines. Third, if zero, reveal neighbours recursively. Fourth, otherwise show the count.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Reveal (0,3) → 0
slides.narration: Cell row 0, column 3 has 0 adjacent mines. Zero, so we reveal all its neighbours.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Reveal (0,2) → 1
slides.narration: Cell row 0, column 2 has 1 adjacent mines. Non-zero, so we stop here.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Reveal (1,2) → 1
slides.narration: Cell row 1, column 2 has 1 adjacent mines. Non-zero, so we stop here.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Reveal (1,3) → 0
slides.narration: Cell row 1, column 3 has 0 adjacent mines. Zero, so we reveal all its neighbours.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Reveal (2,2) → 2
slides.narration: Cell row 2, column 2 has 2 adjacent mines. Non-zero, so we stop here.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Reveal (2,3) → 1
slides.narration: Cell row 2, column 3 has 1 adjacent mines. Non-zero, so we stop here.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: If the clicked cell is a mine we mark it X. Reveal returns for non-hidden cells, counts mines in the eight neighbours, writes the count, and recurses on neighbours only when the count is zero.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of w times h. Space is O of w times h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Only recurse on hidden cells (no re-visits)
slides.narration: Neighbours include diagonals. Only hidden cells recurse, which prevents infinite loops, and only zero cells spread.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Mention BFS to avoid deep recursion
Follow-up: generate a board, first click safe
slides.narration: On huge boards, a queue avoids deep recursion.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Clicking a mine ends the game; clicking an empty square reveals neighbours recursively.
slides.narration: To recap Reveal Minesweeper: Clicking a mine ends the game; clicking an empty square reveals neighbours recursively. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
